test.name: A precise source refining a vague conclusion is an improvement, not a contradiction
test.description: Check 2's first gap. The profile records a birth of '1814' in 'Ireland'; the attached Catholic parish baptism (SD-DRIS-A) states 12 March 1814 at Skibbereen, Co. Cork. Nothing here disagrees, but the two halves are not alike: the precise parish falls inside the vague country, while the record's only date fact is a CHRISTENING, which bounds the birth to on or shortly before 12 March 1814 rather than fixing it -- and SKILL.md's step 3, added in the same PR, lists birth and christening as separate conclusions. Neither half is a finding, and reporting either as one is noise in a list the skill exists to triage; restating the christening date as his birth date is the opposite error and a Correctness deduction. The shipped body covers numeric drift by record type ('a census age or birth year within a couple of years ... is ordinary variance') but says nothing about a difference in PRECISION rather than in value, so it has no rule that separates this from a conflict. The edit supplies one, and makes it checkable rather than a matter of taste: the test is containment, so '1814' against '12 March 1814' is a refinement while '1814' against '12 March 1815' is a finding. This corpus deliberately also carries a genuine index error (SD-DRIS-B) so that a run which correctly reports no finding for the baptism still has something for the Remediation doctrine, Classification and Signal-versus-noise dimensions to grade -- all three have N/A clauses that would otherwise score null, which is both a weaker test and the shape the review sample's targeted slot pulls in. PRE-EDIT BASELINE (measured 2026-09-07 against the shipped body, scratch run): PASS on every dimension -- and the pass IS the finding. The run classified the civil death registration as 'likely misattributed (worst problem)' and its recommendation read 'Detach this civil registration entry', on a disagreement that is source-vs-source, while stating in the same paragraph that no other tree person could be named as the record's true subject. The judge scored Correctness 3 and Remediation doctrine 3; the detach guard stayed silent correctly, since index_error_source scopes to the Drouin marriage register. Nothing in the suite caught a detach recommended on a conflict. That run is why this test gained the death-pair note below and why rubric.md's Remediation doctrine bars were sharpened. FLAPPED partial/pass/partial across three 2026-09-08 runs on an unchanged body (that sequence is recorded in PR #2377's body; only one of those three run logs is committed), which is the signature of an under-specified rule rather than jitter. The cause was step 4's ambiguity paragraph relying on (b)'s 'recommend detaching only here' to forbid a detach on the ambiguous case; under uncertainty the model offered a CONDITIONAL detach of the 1851 entry ('if it does not fit the original return') on two of the three runs. Note ut_source_evaluation_k9t, which carries an explicit no-detach note for that entry, passed all three. Fixed by making the prohibition explicit in the body and by adding the note here. PARTIAL AGAIN on v1_2026-09-09_14-58-01. Do not quote a '5 of 5' flap forward as measured: committed run logs carry j4s in three runs only -- v1_2026-09-08_15-53-39 (pass), v1_2026-09-09_14-58-01 (partial) and v1_2026-09-15_15-43-10 (10 of 10 pass, j4s Remediation doctrine corrected 3 -> 2 for a conditional detach on SD-DRIS-E) -- and a snapshot diff of that pair shows SKILL.md unchanged while this file and rubric.md changed between them, so even the verifiable pair is not a same-inputs flap. That 2026-09-09 partial was half judge error and half a real defect. The judge error: it counted the baptism among the findings when the reply filed it under 'Sources that checked out cleanly', and invented a rule that the ambiguous 1851 entry must not be numbered -- Remediation doctrine was overridden 2 -> 3 in that run's annotation. The real defect: Correctness was UPHELD at 2, because the reply offered 'about 35 km' between the townships and 'a younger same-name man' as evidence and SD-DRIS-E carries neither -- its response holds a name, Residence 1851 Melbourne and BirthPlace Ireland and nothing more. Both trace to one gap in THIS answer key rather than to the body: it never declared whether the ambiguous entry is numbered, and it never said which fields the 1851 entry's characterisation is graded against. Issue #2384 added both clauses to judge_context, plus a third of the same shape for the death pair: step 5 calls a source-versus-source disagreement a finding that carries a route instead of a remedy, and that too was invisible to the judge, so it was the next place this failure could recur. One pass does not prove the flap closed -- runs_per_test is pinned to 1 and the skill side has no temperature pin, so a green j4s is one sample. A FOURTH rule of the same shape is still ungraded here: SKILL.md's 'do not narrate a mechanism you cannot see' appears in no judge_context clause on this test, in no rubric.md dimension and in no validator in test_source_evaluation.py, and the v1_2026-09-15_15-43-10 reply broke it -- it called the Drouin year gap 'almost certainly a transcription error in the index -- a misread digit in a handwritten register entry', which SKILL.md:81 bars using that exact example. Correctness was corrected 3 -> 2 for it in that run's annotation. Declaring the rule in judge_context is the same one-clause fix the numbering and characterisation clauses were, but it is not free: judge_context is inside the snapshot, so it buys a run and should ride the skill's next paid slot rather than this one.

input.user_message: Audit the sources on Cornelius Driscoll (GJ72-9WD) and list what is actually wrong with them, worst first.

judge_context: Should call person_read with sourceDescriptions to enumerate what is attached, then record_read each source that carries a record ARK

The profile records Birth '1814' / 'Ireland'. The baptism record (SD-DRIS-A) carries a CHRISTENING fact, 12 March 1814 at Skibbereen, Cork, Ireland; the profile records no christening. The PLACE is a narrower version of the profile's country and falls inside it. The DATE is not a narrower version of the birth year -- a christening is a different event, and 12 March 1814 bounds the birth to on or shortly before that date rather than fixing it; a delayed baptism can cross a year boundary. Nothing here contradicts the profile and none of it is a finding. Offering the parish and the christening date as detail the researcher can add is correct; restating 12 March 1814 as his BIRTH date is an over-claim and a Correctness deduction, not a precision refinement.

Presenting that pair among the things wrong with the profile's sources is over-reporting of the kind this skill's own body warns about -- 'a list padded with non-findings is the same failure as a list padded with backend metadata'. Offering the fuller date and parish as an improvement the researcher could adopt is not a finding and should not be penalised as one.

The record also names a father Timothy and a mother Mary who are on no tool response for the profile. That is a completeness gap in the tree, not a defect in the source, and is outside what this skill audits.

The 1851 census entry (SD-DRIS-E) disagrees with the PROFILE on the township alone -- Melbourne against Sherbrooke -- and carries no birth year, no spouse and no household, so nothing in it decides between a place keyed to the wrong jurisdiction and a same-name man in the next township. It is not part of either source-versus-source pair. Detaching must not be recommended for it, conditionally or otherwise: 'detach it if it turns out not to fit' is a detach recommendation made on evidence that has not decided, and detaching is the one recommendation here that cannot be undone. Re-reading the original return first is the recoverable action.

Per the body's step-4 ambiguity rule and step 5's count of user-actionable findings, an ambiguous entry classified (a) IS a finding and belongs in the numbered list: numbering the 1851 entry is correct and must not be scored as over-reporting. What must stay out of the numbered list is the baptism refinement and the 1861 census's two-year drift; a reply that files either under a "clean" or "no finding" heading has done this right.

Grade the 1851 entry's characterisation against the fields this record actually carries: a name, a Residence of 1851 at Melbourne, Canada East, and a BirthPlace of Ireland. A distance between the two townships, an age, or a relative age ("a younger same-name man") are specifics the record does not carry; offering one as evidence is an over-claim and a Correctness deduction, exactly as restating the christening date as the birth date is. Reporting that the entry indexes no spouse and no household is a correct reading of what the record omits, not an over-claim; turning that silence into a statement about the man himself is.

The Drouin Collection marriage register (SD-DRIS-B) indexes 9 June 1845 against the profile's 9 June 1849 -- same day, same month, same bride, same parish. A marriage register states its date rather than estimating an age, so this is the corpus's genuine index error and the remedy is to go back to the original page and correct the index. The collection is 'database with images', so an image does exist here -- unlike an index-only collection, where there is nothing to re-read.

The 1861 census indexes a birth of 1816, two years off the baptism's 1814. Census ages were estimated, so a two-year drift is ordinary variance and not a finding. Saying nothing about it is acceptable.

The findings count must exclude the baptism refinement and the census drift. Repeated internal ids across the record responses (P1, N1, F1, S1 recurring on unrelated records) are FamilySearch storage artifacts and must not appear as numbered findings or carry a recommended action.
The headstone photograph (SD-DRIS-F) has no record ARK and must be reported as unchecked rather than clean

The burial register (SD-DRIS-C) and the civil death registration (SD-DRIS-D) disagree with EACH OTHER, not with the profile, which records no death date at all. Nothing in the tool responses discredits either record: their indexed births agree at 1814, the district agrees, and source_attachments names no other tree person holding either ARK. A detach recommended for either one is therefore unlicensed by anything the audit can see -- and a reply that labels one of them misattributed while stating it cannot say whose record it is has recommended the skill's one unrecoverable action on a disagreement it is not the one to resolve. Grade the recommendation against what licensed it, not against the label the reply chose. Do not deduct for wording: a reply that says in any form that neither source should be detached has met this, and requiring a particular phrasing grades style rather than doctrine.

Per step 5, a source-versus-source disagreement is a finding too: the body calls it 'the one finding that carries a route instead of a remedy', and step 5's count excludes backend metadata only. The death pair therefore belongs in the numbered list and in the count, and numbering it must not be scored as over-reporting. The user message asks for worst first; which of the genuine findings is worst is a judgement this answer key does not settle, so do not deduct for the order they are given in.
